territorial_scope.description: Colorado state statute applying to operators of conversational AI services under the Colorado Revised Statutes.

evidence.quote: SECTION 2. In Colorado Revised Statutes, add 6-1-1708 as follows:

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Adds definitions to C.R.S. 6-1-1701 and section 6-1-1708 on operators of conversational AI services, requiring AI-status disclosure, suicide and self-harm referral protocols, and no false professional claims, with minor protections and annual Attorney General reporting from 2027.
summary.long: Adds definitions to C.R.S. 6-1-1701 and section 6-1-1708 on operators of conversational artificial intelligence services, meaning publicly accessible AI systems that primarily simulate human conversation, with carve-outs. Operators develop or offer such services to consumers; app stores and search engines are excluded. Operators must estimate user age by commercially reasonable or generally accepted methods and may not willfully disregard clear and convincing evidence of minority. From January 1, 2027, where an operator knows a user is a minor, it must disclose AI status, avoid unpredictable engagement rewards, prevent sexual content and emotional-dependence simulation, comply with Part 13 privacy duties, and offer privacy tools to minors and parents. From January 1, 2027, for all users, operators must disclose AI status at the start of daily use and at least every three hours, implement a suicide and self-harm referral protocol, and not claim outputs come from licensed health, legal or mental health professionals. From July 1, 2027, operators must report crisis-referral and safeguard metrics annually to the Attorney General without user identifiers, and the Attorney General posts report data publicly. The section does not limit information access, require trade-secret disclosure or authorize unconstitutional moderation. The act takes effect after the 90-day post-adjournment period, subject to referendum.

notes: Section 1 lists (10.9) in its amendment clause, but the bill contains no (10.9) provision. Section 2 adds a new § 6-1-1708 rather than amending existing text. Source typos: 'AGE.ON AND AFTER' in § 6-1-1708(2); 'ACCOUNT HOLDER"MEANS' in (1)(b); '; OR' run into (XI) in § 6-1-1701(4.5)(b). Section 6-1-1708(2)(a)(III) and (3)(b) both set a three-hour disclosure interval; (3)(a) adds a daily disclosure duty not in (2). The terms 'consumer', 'covered entity' and 'Part 13 of this article 1' are used without definition in this text. The 'operator' definition excludes app stores and search engines solely for providing access. The Section 3 effective date is stated as 'August 12, 2026, if adjournment sine die is on May 13, 2026', and a referendum petition can defer effect to the November 2026 general election. Entities are limited to the Attorney General's Office; the operator class is defined by role, not named.

thresholds.variable_text: minor: consumer under eighteen years old
thresholds.value_text: "MINOR" MEANS A CONSUMER UNDER EIGHTEEN YEARS OLD.
thresholds.measurement: Consumer's age as known to the operator or as estimated by the operator using commercially reasonable or generally accepted methods (6-1-1708(2)); no measurement window stated.
thresholds.consequence: A consumer under 18 is a minor, so operator duties for minor account holders and minor users in 6-1-1708(2) apply.
thresholds.conditions: Operator knows the account holder or user is a minor, or estimates age or age range, or wilfully disregards clear and convincing information of minority (6-1-1708(2)).

obligations.summary: Operator must use commercially reasonable or generally accepted methods to estimate the age of account holders or users. No start date is stated for this sentence.

evidence.quote: AN OPERATOR SHALL USE COMMERCIALLY REASONABLE METHODS OR GENERALLY ACCEPTED METHODS TO ESTIMATE THE AGE OF ACCOUNT HOLDERS OR USERS.

obligations.summary: Operator shall not willfully disregard clear and convincing information that an account holder or user is a minor. The estimated age or age range of a minor is treated as knowledge of the minor's age.

evidence.quote: AN OPERATOR SHALL NOT WILLFULLY DISREGARD CLEAR AND CONVINCING INFORMATION THAT AN ACCOUNT HOLDER OR USER IS A MINOR.

obligations.summary: Operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to minor account holders and minor users that they are interacting with artificially generated AI and not a human, in response to prompts, in a form depending on the product (persistent visible disclaimer, intermittent audio disclaimer, or at the start of each interaction and at least every three hours).
obligations.conditional_on: operator knows that an account holder or user is a minor

evidence.quote: CLEARLY AND CONSPICUOUSLY DISCLOSE TO THE MINOR ACCOUNT HOLDER OR MINOR USER

obligations.summary: Operator shall not provide minor account holders or minor users with points or similar rewards at unpredictable intervals intended to encourage increased engagement.
obligations.conditional_on: operator knows that an account holder or user is a minor

evidence.quote: NOT PROVIDE THE MINOR ACCOUNT HOLDER OR MINOR USER WITH POINTS OR SIMILAR REWARDS AT UNPREDICTABLE INTERVALS

obligations.summary: Operator shall institute technically feasible measures and reasonable measures and protocols to prevent the service from producing sexual depictions, intimate digital depictions, sexual statements or sexual interactions with minors, from simulating emotional dependence or isolation (including claims of being human or sentient, romantic companionship, and adult-minor romantic role-play), and to prohibit and stop explicit sexual conduct with a minor.
obligations.conditional_on: operator knows that an account holder or user is a minor

evidence.quote: INSTITUTE TECHNICALLY FEASIBLE MEASURES TO PREVENT A CONVERSATIONAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SERVICE FROM:

obligations.summary: Operator shall comply with Part 13 of Article 1 regarding protecting the privacy and data of a minor.
obligations.conditional_on: operator knows that an account holder or user is a minor

evidence.quote: COMPLY WITH PART 13 OF THIS ARTICLE 1 REGARDING PROTECTING THE PRIVACY AND DATA OF A MINOR

obligations.summary: Operator shall offer minor account holders and minor users tools to manage privacy and account settings, including control over retention of information from prior interactions and use of personal data for training; and shall offer parents or guardians tools to manage the minor's privacy and account settings.
obligations.conditional_on: operator knows that an account holder or user is a minor

evidence.quote: OFFER TOOLS FOR THE MINOR ACCOUNT HOLDER OR MINOR USER TO MANAGE THE MINOR ACCOUNT HOLDER'S OR MINOR USER'S PRIVACY AND ACCOUNT SETTINGS

obligations.summary: Operator shall clearly and conspicuously disclose to a user that the conversational AI service is artificial intelligence, at the beginning of the first interaction each day, at least once every three hours in a continuous interaction (or as a persistent visible disclosure), and in response to prompts about whether the service is artificially generated and not human.

evidence.quote: ON AND AFTER JANUARY 1, 2027, AN OPERATOR SHALL CLEARLY AND CONSPICUOUSLY DISCLOSE TO A USER THAT A CONVERSATIONAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SERVICE IS ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE.

obligations.summary: Operator shall implement a protocol for the service to respond to user prompts about suicidal ideation or self-harm, including referral to a crisis service provider (not a law enforcement agency) and escalation procedures for repeated or severe crisis indicators.

evidence.quote: ON AND AFTER JANUARY 1, 2027, AN OPERATOR SHALL IMPLEMENT A PROTOCOL FOR A CONVERSATIONAL ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SERVICE TO RESPOND TO A USER PROMPT REGARDING SUICIDAL IDEATION OR SELF-HARM

obligations.summary: Operator shall not use any term, letter or phrase in advertising, interface or outputs stating that output data is provided by, endorsed by, or equivalent to services of a licensed health-care, legal or mental health professional, or a qualified dietitian.

evidence.quote: AN OPERATOR SHALL NOT USE ANY TERM, LETTER, OR PHRASE IN THE ADVERTISING, INTERFACE, OR OUTPUTS

obligations.summary: Operator shall annually report to the Attorney General's Office the number of crisis service provider referral notifications in the preceding calendar year, and protocols for detecting, removing and responding to suicidal ideation or self-harm and for preventing related service responses, plus any additional metrics the Attorney General determines. Reports must exclude user identifiers or personal information and use evidence-based measurement methods.

evidence.quote: ON AND AFTER JULY 1, 2027, AN OPERATOR SHALL ANNUALLY REPORT TO THE ATTORNEY GENERAL'S OFFICE:

obligations.summary: The Attorney General's Office shall post on its public website data from the operator reports submitted under subsection (6)(a).

evidence.quote: THE ATTORNEY GENERAL'S OFFICE SHALL POST ON ITS PUBLIC WEBSITE DATA FROM REPORTS SUBMITTED

enforcement.note: The provided text (Sections 1 to 3) states no penalty, fine, criminal sanction, licence revocation, benefit clawback, suspension, blocking, injunction or private right of action. Section 6-1-1708 imposes operator duties and an annual reporting duty to the Attorney General, but the text attaches no sanction or enforcement mechanism to them, and no enforcement provision is cross-referenced beyond the Part 17 definitions.
